results.name: parity_even_minus_odd_asymmetry
results.description: Parity-match effect (yes rate for same-parity minus opposite-parity non-example targets) in all-even sets minus the same effect in all-odd sets (>=2 examples); t_observed differing from null_mean means people treat "even" and "odd" rules asymmetrically, which the model's single shared parity prior cannot capture (above = even rule more favoured than the model allows).
results.code:
# name: parity_even_minus_odd_asymmetry
# description: Parity-match effect (yes rate for same-parity minus opposite-parity non-example targets) in all-even sets minus the same effect in all-odd sets (>=2 examples); t_observed differing from null_mean means people treat "even" and "odd" rules asymmetrically, which the model's single shared parity prior cannot capture (above = even rule more favoured than the model allows).
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    v = ~np.isnan(s); n = v.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    par = np.where(v, s % 2, np.nan)
    pmin = np.nanmin(par, axis=1); pmax = np.nanmax(par, axis=1)
    is_ex = (np.where(v, s, -1) == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    base = (n >= 2) & ~is_ex & (pmin == pmax)
    tp = t % 2
    def eff(p):
        m = base & (pmin == p)
        a = m & (tp == p); b = m & (tp != p)
        if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
            return 0.0
        return r[a].mean() - r[b].mean()
    return float(eff(0) - eff(1))

results.name: cell_mixed_response_fraction
results.description: Fraction of distinct (number_set, target) cells whose repeated answers are not unanimous (some yes, some no); t_observed below null_mean means people agree more (more all-or-none) than the model's graded per-cell probabilities predict, above means they disagree more.
results.code:
# name: cell_mixed_response_fraction
# description: Fraction of distinct (number_set, target) cells whose repeated answers are not unanimous (some yes, some no); t_observed below null_mean means people agree more (more all-or-none) than the model's graded per-cell probabilities predict, above means they disagree more.
def test_statistic(df):
    key = df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(int).astype(str)
    g = df["rating"].astype(float).groupby(key.to_numpy())
    s = g.sum(); n = g.size()
    mixed = (s > 0) & (s < n) & (n > 1)
    denom = (n > 1).sum()
    return float(mixed.sum() / denom) if denom > 0 else 0.0

results.name: inside_outside_range_gap
results.description: In sets with >=2 examples, yes rate for non-example targets inside [min,max] of the examples minus yes rate for targets outside that range; t_observed above null_mean means people fill in the span between examples (interval generalization) more sharply than the model, below means less.
results.code:
# name: inside_outside_range_gap
# description: In sets with >=2 examples, yes rate for non-example targets inside [min,max] of the examples minus yes rate for targets outside that range; t_observed above null_mean means people fill in the span between examples (interval generalization) more sharply than the model, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    v = ~np.isnan(s); n = v.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    lo = np.nanmin(s, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(s, axis=1)
    is_ex = (np.where(v, s, -1) == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    base = (n >= 2) & ~is_ex
    ins = base & (t >= lo) & (t <= hi); out = base & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    if ins.sum() == 0 or out.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[ins].mean() - r[out].mean())

results.name: round_number_target_excess
results.description: In sets whose examples do not all end in 0, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of 10 minus other non-example targets at the same nearest-example distance band (>5 away); t_observed above null_mean means people over-endorse round numbers relative to the model, below means they avoid them more.
results.code:
# name: round_number_target_excess
# description: In sets whose examples do not all end in 0, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of 10 minus other non-example targets at the same nearest-example distance band (>5 away); t_observed above null_mean means people over-endorse round numbers relative to the model, below means they avoid them more.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    v = ~np.isnan(s)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    tf = t.astype(float)
    all0 = ((np.where(v, s % 10, 0) == 0)).all(axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(s - tf[:, None]), axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    base = ~all0 & (dist > 5)
    a = base & (t % 10 == 0); b = base & (t % 10 != 0)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: single_example_near_far_gap
results.description: In one-example sets, yes rate for targets 1-10 from the example minus yes rate for targets >10 away; t_observed above null_mean means people's generalization from a single example is more local (similarity-based) than the model predicts, below means flatter/more rule-based.
results.code:
# name: single_example_near_far_gap
# description: In one-example sets, yes rate for targets 1-10 from the example minus yes rate for targets >10 away; t_observed above null_mean means people's generalization from a single example is more local (similarity-based) than the model predicts, below means flatter/more rule-based.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    n = s.str.count(",").to_numpy() + 1
    x = pd.to_numeric(s.str.split(",").str[0], errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    d = np.abs(t - x)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a = (n == 1) & (d >= 1) & (d <= 10); b = (n == 1) & (d > 10)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: power_of_two_set_specificity
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples all in {2,4,8,16,32,64}, yes rate for non-example power-of-two targets minus yes rate for other even targets; t_observed above null_mean means people pick out the powers-of-two rule more sharply than the model's shared "powers" family prior allows, below means less.
results.code:
# name: power_of_two_set_specificity
# description: In sets of >=2 examples all in {2,4,8,16,32,64}, yes rate for non-example power-of-two targets minus yes rate for other even targets; t_observed above null_mean means people pick out the powers-of-two rule more sharply than the model's shared "powers" family prior allows, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    v = ~np.isnan(s); n = v.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    p2 = np.array([2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64], dtype=float)
    ex_p2 = (np.isin(s, p2) | ~v).all(axis=1)
    is_ex = (np.where(v, s, -1) == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    tp2 = np.isin(t, p2.astype(int))
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    base = (n >= 2) & ex_p2 & ~is_ex
    a = base & tp2; b = base & ~tp2 & (t % 2 == 0)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: common_contained_digit_far_yes_rate
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples that all contain some digit d, yes rate for targets containing d that share no final digit with any example and are >10 from every example; t_observed above null_mean means people use "contains digit d" more than the model's (down-weighted) contains-digit family predicts, below means less.
results.code:
# name: common_contained_digit_far_yes_rate
# description: In sets of >=2 examples that all contain some digit d, yes rate for targets containing d that share no final digit with any example and are >10 from every example; t_observed above null_mean means people use "contains digit d" more than the model's (down-weighted) contains-digit family predicts, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    v = ~np.isnan(s); n = v.sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    tf = t.astype(float)
    sv = np.where(v, s, 0).astype(int)
    common_hit = np.zeros(len(t), dtype=bool)
    for d in range(10):
        # digit d appears in number x (1..100)
        def has(x):
            tens = x // 10 % 10; ones = x % 10; hund = x // 100
            return (ones == d) | ((tens == d) & (x >= 10)) | ((hund == d) & (x >= 100))
        all_have = (has(sv) | ~v).all(axis=1)
        common_hit |= all_have & has(t)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(s - tf[:, None]), axis=1)
    last_share = (np.where(v, sv % 10, -1) == (t % 10)[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    m = (n >= 2) & common_hit & ~last_share & (dist > 10)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[m].mean())

results.name: same_decade_near_gap
results.description: Among non-example targets 1-9 from the nearest example, yes rate when the target shares its tens digit (decade, n//10) with some example minus when it does not; t_observed above null_mean means people generalize within decades more than the model's distance-only intervals predict.
results.code:
# name: same_decade_near_gap
# description: Among non-example targets 1-9 from the nearest example, yes rate when the target shares its tens digit (decade, n//10) with some example minus when it does not; t_observed above null_mean means people generalize within decades more than the model's distance-only intervals predict.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    v = ~np.isnan(s)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(s - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    sd = (np.where(v, s // 10, -99) == (t // 10)[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    base = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 9)
    a = base & sd; b = base & ~sd
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
